title: Sharpening transfers saturated towers and functorial desingularization rules
statement:
Let $M$ be a fine torsion-free monoscheme and $M^\sharp$ its sharp fan [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] and [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Image under $\lambda:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M/\mathcal M^\times$ bijects coherent ideals on $M$ with coherent ideals on $M^\sharp$. Sharpening identifies the corresponding saturated blowups and hence the finite ordered saturated blowup towers, preserving nonempty centers, unit-ideal stages, smoothness of the final object, and pullback along smooth maps.

More generally, sharpening induces a natural bijection between saturated desingularization rules on all fine torsion-free monoschemes with finite affine covers and such rules on all fine torsion-free fans with finite affine covers, when both rules are functorial for smooth maps by contracted pullback, with their ideal centers and order. This bijection preserves identity and composition compatibility. It is defined locally even for fans with no global monoscheme lift: an affine fan lifts to the monoscheme of its sharp monoid, and the rule on a finite affine cover is recovered by gluing the uncontracted restrictions of the rule on their finite disjoint union. In particular the resulting fan tower is finite and independent of the affine cover.
